stem.en: Why do taller plants need specialised transport tissues?

text.en: Their upper parts are far from the water at the roots.

feedback.en: Yes. Water cannot reach a high leaf simply by passing across the surface, as it does in Spirogyra.

text.en: Their cells have no walls, so they lose water very quickly.

feedback.en: Plant cells have rigid walls of cellulose, whatever the height of the plant.

text.en: Their leaves cannot make food without pipes to bring it.

feedback.en: Leaves make the food. Phloem carries that food to other parts of the plant.

text.en: Only tall plants need water to reach their seeds and fruits.

feedback.en: Ferns have no seeds, and they still have transport tissue.

explanation.en: A thread of Spirogyra touches water at every cell. In a tall plant, the leaves are far from the water at the roots and the roots are far from the food made in the leaves, so xylem and phloem carry them.

hints.en: Compare a leaf at the top of a tree with a cell of Spirogyra.
